definitions.explanation: Sake brewed using only rice, water, rice koji, and yeast, with no added distilled alcohol.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{純米酒|じゅんまいしゅ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧おいしい。
{純米酒|じゅんまいしゅ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{米|こめ}→米：01323_kome⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{味|あじ}→味：00826_aji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦しっかり→しっかり：01272_shikkari⟧⟦{感|かん}じられる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: With junmai sake, you can really taste the rice.

examples.japanese: ⟦{地元|じもと}→地元：09941_jimoto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{酒蔵|さかぐら}→酒蔵：08633_sakagura⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{造|つく}られた→造る：17751_tsukuru⟧{純米酒|じゅんまいしゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{土産|みやげ}→土産：03746_miyage⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought a junmai sake made at a local brewery as a souvenir.

notes:
A compound of {純米|じゅんまい} (pure rice) and {酒|しゅ} (sake/alcohol). Junmai sake is distinguished from other sake categories by the absence of added ⟦{醸造|じょうぞう}→醸造：14438_jouzou⟧⟦アルコール→アルコール：01771_arukooru⟧ (distilled alcohol). This gives it a fuller, richer body with more pronounced rice flavor.

SAKE CLASSIFICATION HIERARCHY:
- {純米酒|じゅんまいしゅ}: pure rice sake (no polishing ratio requirement)
- {純米吟醸酒|じゅんまいぎんじょうしゅ}: pure rice ginjo (rice polished to 60% or less)
- {純米大吟醸酒|じゅんまいだいぎんじょうしゅ}: pure rice daiginjo (rice polished to 50% or less)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{辛口|からくち}→辛口：18794_karakuchi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{純米酒|じゅんまいしゅ}: dry junmai sake
- ⟦{甘口|あまくち}→甘口：18197_amakuchi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{純米酒|じゅんまいしゅ}: sweet junmai sake
- ⟦{冷|ひ}や→冷や：28141_hiya⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧: to drink chilled
- {燗|かん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つける→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧: to warm (sake)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Junmai sake can be enjoyed at a wide range of temperatures, from chilled to warmed. Its robust flavor makes it especially popular for pairing with food.
